henry.title: Bagpipe Drones, Ukulele and String Detective
henry.intro: Bagpipes make a steady hum called a drone while the tune plays on top. Today you'll make your own drone on the ukulele and explore the strings on the guitar and cello. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: FIRST (2 min): watch the 1-minute video (link). Listen for the drone hum and the tune.
NEXT (6 min): open 'Show me how: Drone on your uke'. Do steps 1 to 4.
THEN (5 min): open 'Show me how: String detective' and do steps 1 to 4 with the guitar and cello (a grown-up helps with the cello).
LAST (2 min): answer questions 1 to 5. Done when you can play the drone and sing for 8 beats!
links: Video: What Is a Bagpipe? (1 minute)
Watch and listen for the drone and the tune.

handsOn.title: 🎸 Drone on your uke + String detective
steps: guides/uke-c-chord.svg
Drone: Make your C chord from last week (ring finger on the A string, fret 3).
guides/uke-c-chord.svg
Strum slowly: down, down, rest, down (X X - X). Keep it going. That steady sound is your drone.
guides/uke-c-chord.svg
Tune on top: Keep strumming and sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat'. The C chord fits the whole song! Then try the first line of 'Auld Lang Syne': 'Should auld acquaintance be forgot'.
guides/uke-c-chord.svg
Count how many beats you kept the drone going without stopping.
guides/strings-compare.svg
Guitar and cello: Pluck each open string on the guitar from thickest to thinnest. Listen: which is lowest?
guides/strings-compare.svg
Pluck the cello strings too (grown-up helps). Which is thickest? Does it sound low or high?
guides/strings-compare.svg
Pluck one string. Now press your finger halfway down the neck on that string and pluck again. A shorter string sounds higher or lower?
guides/strings-compare.svg
Write what you heard on the worksheet.
handsOn.look: Thick strings make low sounds. Short strings make high sounds. The drone is the steady sound underneath a tune.

worksheet: A drone is a ________ sound that keeps going while the tune plays. Circle: STEADY / QUICK
How many beats did your uke drone last without stopping? ___
On the guitar, the thickest string sounds ______ (low / high). The thinnest sounds ______.
When you pressed halfway down a string, the sound got ______ (higher / lower).
Which instrument is the biggest of the four (piano, ukulele, guitar, cello)? ________ Does it make the lowest sounds? YES / NO

frankie.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb with a Drone 🎹🐑
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: Bagpipes hum one steady sound called a drone while the tune plays. We'll do that on the piano! (About 12 minutes.)
steps: Grown-up: put the colored stickers back on the 5 keys like last Thursday (🟤1 🟢2 🟡3 🟠4 🔴5).
Grown-up: hold down the LOW brown 1 key (the drone). Frankie plays the tune from the picture with one finger, going left to right.
Swap! Frankie holds the drone and the grown-up plays the tune.
Crayons: color a tartan on the worksheet. Done!

handsOn.title: 🎹 Piano drone song
steps: guides/song-numbers.svg
👀 Look at the colored dots. They match your key stickers.
guides/song-numbers.svg
👆 Press the dots in order: 3 2 1 2 3 3 3 · 2 2 2 · 3 5 5 🐑
guides/song-numbers.svg
🤝 A grown-up holds the low 1 the whole time: the drone!
handsOn.look: Grown-up: the tune is 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'. Sing it together.
handsOn.q: Color the dots on your sheet.

worksheet: Color the dots to match your stickers. 🟤1 🟢2 🟡3 🟠4 🔴5
Color a tartan: first color every row with stripes (red, blue), then color the columns (green, yellow).
